content.text:
Reference image 1 shows a lion. Use it only for the head and tail.
Reference image 2 shows a bald eagle. Use it only for the torso, limbs and skin covering.
Create one new creature with a single, committed biped body plan.
Place the lion's head and tail on the bald eagle's frame so every join heals naturally: no visible seams, no floating parts, no duplicated limbs.
A fusion with a body_plan conflict (e.g. finned x quadruped with no amphibious design note) must be flagged, not silently resolved by picking one parent's plan.
Show the full body in a calm three-quarter view on a plain, softly lit background, in the style of a natural history field-guide plate. Photographic realism, accurate anatomy, no text, no labels, no people.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Fusing lion and eagle anatomy**
I'm planning a photorealistic field-guide plate that places the lion's head and tail onto the bald eagle's torso and limbs, forming a single biped with seamless joins, shown in a calm three-quarter view on a plain, softly lit background.
**Composing hybrid creature image**
I'm planning a natural-history field guide illustration in 3/4 view, merging an eagle's body, wings, legs and talons with a lion's head, mane and tufted tail, on a plain softly lit background with seamless brown feathering.
**Refining hybrid creature design**
I'm removing the eagle tail feathers so only the lion tail remains, then regenerating the image to match the requested hybrid look.
